head: b72e11b626aeef613e0022809c0d39c782947865
summary:
Fail. At this head, no linked issue is closed automatically after a real asynchronous native merge, so issue #115's outcome is not delivered.

What is met:
- Guarded close (`guarded_close`, `post_merge_observation`) closes only the exact merged PR's single linked issue. It checks the merge parent and default-branch ancestry.
- Before writing, it rechecks the issue contract, labels, assignees, ownership timeline seal and guard owner, and never takes over a later claim. Unknown evidence keeps the issue open.
- Synthetic controls cover asynchronous merge, already-closed issue, delayed merge, provider failure, stale head or base, changed issue, unrelated PR, duplicate wake and recovery.
- Existing CI, performance, review, protected-branch, no-bypass and return-to-todo gates are preserved.
- No schedule is deployed and other sessions' worktrees are untouched.
- New at this head: the native writer and the adoption publisher bind the mutation's client ID to the guard intent. A missing or mismatched ID blocks the success status.

What still blocks:
1. `recovery_entry.verify_rollout` always refuses, so every guarded path stops before any write.
2. A later wake can permanently block a queued guarded PR. The first run keeps the guard, `begin` fails on the next wake, and `block_unadmitted` posts a pending status over the queued PR's success. Nothing restores it.
3. No real hosted asynchronous merge has closed its issue automatically. The Core #77 fixture records a manual close.
4. The controlled hosted comparison of the `issues: write` permission hypothesis is absent.
5. Actor and launcher adoption, request ownership and safe cancellation remain unproven.

Hosted controls run 40940853574 passed 861 tests with no skips. Do not merge or deploy this draft; issue #115 stays todo.

findings.title: Verified post-merge closure remains unreachable
findings.detail: `verify_rollout` always raises `recovery_rollout_not_verified`. `native_merge.main`, `adoption_guard.begin`, `policy_adoption_target_review.preflight` and `recovery_entry.main` all stop before any guarded write, so no issue is closed after an asynchronous native merge.
findings.required_fix: Implement and review a rollout-evidence verifier bound to the exact policy and runtime. Deploy recovery through the reviewed policy-adoption process and demonstrate an automatic close.

findings.title: Later wake permanently blocks a queued guarded PR
findings.detail: After a guarded enqueue reports queued, the guard is retained. On the next wake, `guarded.begin` fails because the guard is held, and `reconcile` calls `block_unadmitted`. That posts a pending `claude/verified-merge` status over the queued PR's success. No path restores success, so the native merge never completes. The client-ID acknowledgement added at this head does not change this.
findings.required_fix: Bind the queued request and its success status to the guard owner. Skip re-blocking a PR whose authenticated owner holds a live queued request, or implement a safe re-verification path. Add consecutive-wake controls for a queued PR.

findings.title: No hosted asynchronous automatic-close proof or permission comparison
findings.detail: All controls are synthetic, and the Core #77 fixture records a manual close. The controlled hosted comparison of the `issues: write` hypothesis that the issue requires is absent.
findings.required_fix: Run hosted positive and negative asynchronous merge controls in which the linked issue is closed. Run the controlled `issues: write` comparison before changing any production permission.

findings.title: Actor and launcher adoption and request ownership unproven
findings.detail: `actor_rollout` is always 'unknown'. `cancel_blocked` keeps every existing request because the shared Actions bot identity cannot prove which run created it. Cancellation and its race with merging are not implemented.
findings.required_fix: Provide verified actor and launcher adoption evidence and authenticated request provenance bound to the guard, with positive and negative controls.
